## Summary

<!-- In a short paragraph, usually two to four sentences, explain the
problem in plain English: who or what is affected, what is wrong, missing,
or unnecessarily difficult, and why that matters.

Assume the reader knows what the project does but has not followed this
work. Use familiar words. Leave internal names, unexplained acronyms,
architecture, and implementation details for the sections below. -->

## Goal and motivation

<!-- State the improvement or decision this PR is meant to achieve.
Build on the Summary with the evidence, established cause, or constraints
that explain why this goal is worth pursuing.

Use the request, issue, and verified evidence. Do not invent benefits or
infer the motivation from the diff alone. Explain useful context without
repeating the opening, and distinguish facts from assumptions. -->

## Expected outcome

<!-- Explain what should be possible or different when this work is
complete. Give observable conditions that a reviewer can check, using
a short before/after example when helpful. Include scope and meaningful
limitations.

State which outcomes this PR delivers, proposes, or leaves for follow-up.
Keep expected benefits separate from measured results. Link required
companion changes and relevant remaining work.

Add brief implementation notes only when they help explain how the
approach achieves the outcome or affects its risks. -->

## Risks and compatibility

<!-- Describe material compatibility, data, safety, configuration, or
deployment effects. Include required component versions, upgrade ordering,
migration, or recovery guidance where relevant.

If no material risk is expected, briefly explain why that follows from
the scope. -->

## Verification

<!-- Connect the checks to the expected outcomes and material risks.
Report what actually ran, the observed results, and what remains
unverified. Include relevant commands, environment details, test references,
or CI links.

Distinguish passed, failed, not run, and not applicable. Keep planned
checks separate from completed evidence.

Add manual steps only when they provide useful additional verification.
State the setup, expected result, whether the check was performed, and
cleanup when it changes persistent state. -->
